case: One registered predicate is given a genuine second `implementation_status` -- a classification that is NOT the negative-fixture sentinel -- which must still trip the F6D-09 tripwire.
why: The F6D-09 tripwire exists to fire the moment the predicate registry gains an implementation-status classification, because that is the moment the review's third clause -- a conjunct asserting each named precondition predicate is deterministic -- stops being vacuous and becomes writable. r7-contracts-b had to exclude the negative-fixture sentinel from it, since a fixture that ADDS a predicate must give that predicate a status and was tripping the tripwire inside its own scratch tree. An exclusion is a hole until something proves it is the right size. This fixture is that proof from the adverse side: a second value that is not the sentinel, on a predicate that really is in the contract, and the tripwire must still see it. Its benign twin proves the other side.
expect_failure_contains: THE PREDICATE REGISTRY NOW CLASSIFIES IMPLEMENTATION STATUS

patch.value: implemented; deterministic evaluator bound in production
